extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, affected landowners, Tribes, state/local agencies, and other stakeholders invited to comment on FERC's NEPA scoping for the Cedar Vale Compressor Station Project
extracted.subtask_short: FERC scoping comments for pipeline project
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting scoping comments and participating in the FERC NEPA review for the proposed Cedar Vale Compressor Station (Docket No. CP25-19-000). Includes what topics to address, how to file, deadlines, cooperating agency and Section 106 consultation information, and mailing-list procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments should focus on the potential environmental effects, reasonable alternatives, and measures to avoid or lessen environmental impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input will help Commission staff determine what issues to evaluate in the environmental document; staff will consider all written comments during preparation. The main goal of scoping is to focus analysis on important environmental issues and potentially eliminate others from further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and receipt of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted so the Commission receives them in Washington, DC on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, June 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure comments are timely and properly recorded, meet the stated receipt deadline. If you submitted comments before the opening of this docket (before Nov 18, 2024), you must file those comments in Docket No. CP25-19-000 for them to be considered in this proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable submission methods and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods are provided to submit comments: (1) eComment (brief, text-only comments via FERC Online), (2) eFiling (electronic filing allowing attachments), and (3) paper mail sent to specified Commission addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eComment is an easy method for brief text-only comments. eFiling allows attachments; new eFiling users must create an account via eRegister and select the filing type 'Comment on a Filing.' Paper submissions must reference the docket number (CP25-19-000) and use the specified USPS or carrier addresses. Follow the provided instructions carefully so comments are properly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the docket number and address instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should reference Docket No. CP25-19-000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing paper comments, include the docket number on your letter. Use the USPS address for Postal Service mail and the alternate Rockville/carrier address for other carriers. Failure to reference the docket or use the proper address may affect recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics / NEPA resource areas to address
rubrics_metrics.description: The environmental document will discuss impacts in the following general resource areas: geology and soils; water resources and wetlands; vegetation and wildlife; threatened and endangered species; cultural resources; land use; socioeconomics; environmental justice; air quality and noise; and reliability and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that address these resource areas (or identify other potentially relevant issues) will help staff identify and focus issues that might affect the human environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on alternatives and alternate locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplemental Notice specifically requests comments on alternate compressor station locations (Alternatives A and B, submitted by Southern Star, and Alternative C identified by Commission staff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission staff are assessing potential impacts of the proposed location and the three alternate locations; comments about the comparative impacts, siting, and reasonable alternatives will inform the environmental analysis. See Appendix 1/appendices in eLibrary for maps and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting cooperating agency status / agency participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies with jurisdiction by law and/or special expertise regarding environmental issues of the project are asked to formally cooperate in the preparation of the environmental document and may request cooperating agency status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies that wish to request cooperating agency status should follow the comment-filing instructions in the Public Participation section. The Council on Environmental Quality regulations on cooperating agency responsibilities are at 40 CFR 1501.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106 consultation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice initiates consultation under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act: FERC will consult with applicable State Historic Preservation Offices, interested Indian tribes, and other agencies and the public on potential effects to historic properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The environmental document will document findings on impacts to historic properties and summarize the status of Section 106 consultations. The Advisory Council on Historic Preservation's implementing regulations are at 36 CFR part 800, which define historic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental mailing list inclusion and update procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The environmental mailing list includes federal, state, and local government representatives and agencies; elected officials; environmental and public interest groups; Native American Tribes; other interested parties; local libraries and newspapers; affected landowners; and anyone who submits comments and provides a mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change your name/address or remove yourself from the mailing list, either email GasProjectAddressChange@ferc.gov (include docket number CP25-19-000 and the name/address as it appeared on the notice) or return the attached Mailing List Update Form (appendix 2). Note: the GasProjectAddressChange email address cannot accept comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landowner easement and eminent domain information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a landowner, you may be contacted about acquisition of an easement to construct, operate, and maintain facilities; you are not required to enter into an agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission approves the project and an easement agreement is not reached, the Natural Gas Act conveys the right of eminent domain to the company, which could initiate condemnation proceedings in court; compensation would be determined by a judge under state law. The Commission does not exercise jurisdiction over eminent domain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment (EA) review and comment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff will prepare an Environmental Assessment (EA) for the project; the EA may be issued for an allotted public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will consider timely comments on the EA before making its decision regarding the proposed project. The EA will be available electronically through eLibrary and on FERC's natural gas environmental documents web page; eSubscription notifies subscribers when documents are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: How comments are used in scoping and document preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping gathers public and agency input to focus the environmental document's analysis on important environmental issues and to identify issues that may be eliminated from further study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments help Commission staff identify and focus on issues that might have an effect on the human environment and potentially eliminate other issues from further study and discussion in the environmental document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance and contact resources for participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission offers support to help members of the public participate and make filings: FERC Online Support, the Office of Public Participation (OPP), and the Office of External Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact FERC Online Support for eLibrary/eFiling assistance at FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov or (866) 208-3676 (TTY (202) 502-8659). OPP can help with filings, interventions, and navigating Commission processes at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov. The Office of External Affairs (866) 208-FERC also provides project information.
